bull.argument: COST shows durable growth and financial strength in this filing. Net sales rose 10% to $297,247 million, with comparable sales up 8% and digitally-enabled comparable sales up 21%. Membership fee revenue grew 11% to $5,907 million, and renewal rates held at 92.3% in the U.S. and Canada. Net income increased 14% to $9,226 million, and operating cash flow climbed to $15,817 million from $13,335 million. Management is also reinvesting in the franchise: capital expenditures were $6,435 million in 2026, with about $7,500 million planned for 2027 and up to 33 new warehouses. The balance sheet supports this, with $21,301 million in cash and short-term investments and a 13% dividend increase. The risk factors are real, particularly the concentration in U.S. and California operations and the rising cost of AI and cybersecurity, but the filing shows a business that has absorbed these pressures while growing earnings and cash generation. The IEEPA tariff refunds of $184 million are a further, though modest, tailwind.

claims.claim: Membership fee revenue growth and member loyalty are strong.
claims.quote: Membership fee revenue increased 11% to $5,907, driven by new member sign-ups, membership fee increases, and upgrades to Executive membership
Digitally-enabled comparable sales increased 21% during 2026, both as reported and excluding the impact of changes in foreign currencies.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow and liquidity strengthened.
claims.quote: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $15,817 in 2026, compared to $13,335 in 2025.

bear.argument: The bull case rests on growth that the filing ties to fragile sources. Net sales rose 10%, but the filing says gasoline added $3,501 million, about 130 basis points, and currency added $1,332 million. Strip out those external tailwinds and the growth is far less impressive. Gross margin fell three basis points to 11.09%, and the filing notes that the 10 basis point improvement appears only after excluding gasoline inflation. Management also says the business 'operates on very low margins,' so small cost swings matter a lot. Concentration is another problem. The U.S. and Canada produce 86% and 83% of net sales and operating income, and California alone is 26% of U.S. sales. Capital spending is rising to about $7,500 million, with up to 33 openings, while the filing warns that new sites may be less profitable and may cannibalize existing warehouses. The 13% dividend increase and $847 million of buybacks also draw on that heavy spending plan.

claims.claim: Gasoline inflation contributed a large share of reported sales growth.
claims.quote: Higher gasoline prices positively impacted net sales by $3,501, or 130 basis points

claims.claim: Gross margin percentage declined on a reported basis, and the improvement appears only after adjusting for gasoline.
claims.quote: Gross margin percentage decreased three basis points; it increased 10 basis points excluding the impact of gasoline price inflation

claims.claim: Earnings depend heavily on a few regions, with California a concentrated exposure.
claims.quote: Within the U.S., we are highly dependent on our California operations, which comprised 26% of U.S. net sales in 2026.

bull.argument: The opponent's strongest point, that gasoline and currency flattered growth, is fair, but the filing shows the core business still grew. Comparable sales rose 8%, and excluding foreign-currency and gasoline effects they still rose 7%, in both the U.S. and Canada. Core merchandise sales rose $17,136 million, increasing in all categories, so growth is not only a fuel story. Gross margin fell only three basis points, and management says the core category margin as a share of its own sales rose 15 basis points. Operating cash flow of $15,817 million, up from $13,335 million, and cash and short-term investments of $21,301 million cover the $7,500 million capital plan and the dividend without strain. Concentration and cannibalization are real risks the filing discloses, but they are the price of a cash-generating franchise, not evidence of weakness. The filing also records a 13% dividend increase, which a board would not approve for a business it expected to falter.

claims.claim: Core growth persists after stripping out gasoline and currency effects.
claims.quote: Increases in comparable sales excluding the impact of changes in foreign-currency and gasoline prices (1) : U.S. 7 % 7 % 5 %

claims.claim: Core merchandise margins improved even though total margin dipped slightly.
claims.quote: The gross margin in core merchandise categories when expressed as a percentage of their own sales increased 15 basis points.

claims.claim: Cash generation and liquidity fund the investment plan.
claims.quote: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled $15,817 in 2026, compared to $13,335 in 2025.

bear.argument: The opponent's best evidence is real, but it does not settle the risk question. Yes, comparable sales excluding currency and gasoline rose 7%. But the filing also shows that the core-category gross margin improvement is offset in the reported figures: core merchandise margin fell 11 basis points as a share of total sales, and the filing attributes that to mix shift and co-brand card reward costs tied to gasoline. Growth is more fuel-dependent than the headline suggests. Operating cash flow and cash balances are strong, but the filing says the $21,301 million includes $2,842 million of unsettled card receivables, and that 'a small percentage' of IEEPA refunds may be delayed. The cash plan also rests on expansion the filing calls uncertain: 'There can be no assurance that current expectations will be realized.' Management itself warns that new warehouses carry lower initial profitability and may cannibalize existing sites. A dividend increase and buybacks are shareholder returns, not proof of durability. Growth funded by heavy capex, in a business the filing says 'operates on very low margins,' leaves little room for error.

claims.claim: Core merchandise margin fell as a share of total sales, partly because of mix and gasoline-linked card rewards.
claims.quote: Core merchandise categories were also negatively impacted by our co-branded credit card program as a result of reward costs associated with higher gasoline sales.

claims.claim: The capital plan carries explicit uncertainty about whether expected spending and openings will occur.
claims.quote: There can be no assurance that current expectations will be realized, and plans are subject to change

claims.claim: The business runs on thin margins, so small cost changes can have large effects on earnings.
claims.quote: Because our business operates on very low margins, modest changes in various items in the consolidated statements of income, particularly merchandise costs and SG&A expenses, can have substantial impacts on net income.

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes, but the bear's evidence is more pointed: it ties the headline growth to gasoline and currency, and cites verified language on thin margins and no-assurance on expansion. The bull responds well by showing core comparable sales ex-gasoline and currency still rose 7%, but it leans on cash flow and the dividend without fully rebutting the margin-mix and cannibalization risks the bear raised. The bear edges out the win on responsiveness and evidence specificity.
